source_families: Federal Reserve Board Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking (SHED)
U.S. Department of Agriculture Economic Research Service, Household Food Security in the United States
directional_readout: The independent U.S. series do not move identically: both SHED adult measures are flat from 2022 to 2024, USDA household food insecurity rises slightly, and JPMorganChase reports a higher household cash-liquidity endpoint when disposable income and short-term credit are included. Together they show construct-dependent, non-uniform resource pressure, not a common trend estimate.
blocking_items: SHED is adult-level while USDA and JPMorganChase are household-level
different questionnaires, administrative methods, and sampling frames
USDA 2024 change is not statistically significant versus 2023
JPMorganChase combines cash, disposable income, and short-term credit in its broader endpoint
year-specific uncertainty intervals are not attached to the SHED chart series

uncertainty_audit.shed: The public chart artifact supplies point estimates only; the 2024 codebook identifies 12,295 respondents, but no interval was attached to either normalized SHED series.
uncertainty_audit.usda: USDA publishes statistical-significance guidance and calculates standard errors with balanced repeated replication; the 2022-2024 national points are not statistically distinguishable on the published comparison.
uncertainty_audit.use: Keep the comparison descriptive and unpooled until year-specific intervals or a reproducible variance extract is attached to both series.

next_action: Attach year-specific uncertainty intervals or a reproducible variance extract and preserve JPMorganChase licensing limits before any quantitative comparison; keep this lane as a mechanism challenge in the meantime.
boundary: Independent sources can converge directionally without measuring the same population outcome. No pooling or trend promotion is authorized.
